meta.title: Operation of Pulverizer in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To reduce the particle size of crude drugs and plant materials to a uniform powder suitable for extraction, standardization, and phytochemical screening.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for size reduction of dried plant materials, bark, roots, seeds, and resins before further processing.
procedure: Ensure the crude drug material is thoroughly dried before pulverization — moisture content above 10% clogs the pulverizer.
Inspect the pulverizer blades, chamber, and discharge sieve for cleanliness and absence of previous material residue.
Select and fix the appropriate mesh sieve at the discharge outlet as per required particle size.
Break large lumps of dried plant material manually into smaller pieces (< 2 cm) before loading.
Load the dried plant material into the pulverizer hopper — do not exceed the rated capacity (typically 500 g per batch).
Ensure the collection vessel is properly fitted at the outlet before switching ON.
Switch on the pulverizer and allow it to reach full operating speed before feeding material continuously.
Collect the powder from the discharge outlet in a clean, dry, labelled container.
After processing, switch OFF and allow the blades to come to a complete stop before opening the chamber.
Remove remaining material from the chamber using a soft brush — do not use metal tools near the blades.
Clean the chamber, sieve, and blades with a dry brush followed by compressed air; wash with water if switching materials.
Pass the collected powder through the target mesh sieve manually to verify particle size uniformity.
Label the powder with plant name, part used, date of pulverization, and batch number.
Record batch details, weight before and after pulverization, and sieve size used in the logbook.
precautions: Wear a dust mask (N95), safety goggles, and gloves during operation — plant dust can be allergenic.
Never insert hands or any object into the pulverizer chamber during operation.
Do not overload — excess material causes motor overheating and blade damage.
Ensure the material is completely dry — wet material clogs the sieve and damages the motor.
Woody and fibrous materials (e.g., bark, roots) may require pre-cutting with a cutter mill first.
Clean the pulverizer thoroughly between different plant materials to avoid cross-contamination.
Inspect blades for wear, nicks, or damage before each use — replace worn blades immediately.
Ground the pulverizer to prevent static charge buildup when processing fine powders.
